text: This prospective comparison applies the frozen project coding specifications 0.3 and 0.4 to identical source packets. Version 0.4 changes the project’s evidence and representation conventions; it does not change the official Institutional Grammar 2.0 framework. The comparison concerns complete coding workflows, including their schemas and checkers, rather than the isolated effect of codebook wording.

The canonical corpus contains 25,508 Bitcoin Core pull-request records. A conservative inventory excluded 226 previously exposed or referenced PRs found in the retained project material. Eligible records contained 1,000–12,000 Unicode characters across the complete body, comments, reviews, and inline comments, including bots and quotations. The title and serialized metadata did not contribute to this size criterion. A frozen SHA-256 ranking selected one record from each of three metadata strata: procedure-related title, remaining merged contribution, and remaining closed-unmerged contribution. The procedure stratum took precedence. These are sampling proxies, not substantive governance classifications.

The selected cases are fresh relative to the retained project exposure inventory. Unrecorded prior inspection and model training exposure cannot be excluded. The evidence package retains the selection rules, candidate ranks, exclusions, selected corpus lines, hashes, and a verification script. No candidate was selected for a favorable coding result.

The packets preserve all 49 original entries, including empty entries, and add 34 common contextual entries. Supplements contain recorded outcomes, relevant patches, directly referenced commits, a contribution guide pinned to a recorded revision, and separate metadata for the explicitly referenced successor PR. All six coders for a case received the same packet bytes. Missing edit histories, thread referents, image contents, and unprovided documents remain evidence limits.

Each version received three independent runs per case, for eighteen annotations. Every run used a fresh context without parent conversation, earlier annotations, or other coders’ output. Dispatch alternated the two conditions within cases and rotated their starting order. All runs used the inherited primary configuration without a model or reasoning override. The interface did not expose a provider snapshot, seed, sampling parameters, token count, or cost; those fields remain null. This is a same-configuration comparison, not cross-model validation.

Each coder preserved its first complete annotation, received mechanical checker feedback, conducted one source-based self-review, and froze its final annotation and change log. Mechanical checks assess schema consistency, source offsets, references, and specified safeguards. They cannot establish whether an institutional interpretation follows from the cited source.

A separate alignment context receives source packets and shuffled annotation aliases with direct classification fields withheld. Two fresh source-review contexts receive the full aliased records and their assigned coding guides, without aggregate agreement scores or the other reviewer’s findings. Structural differences can reveal the applicable conventions, so masking is partial. The coordinator reconciles the independent review findings against the source and retains unresolved judgments. This source-review process provides revisable analytical judgments, not a human reference dataset or an accuracy standard.

The primary assessment distinguishes interpretation-changing errors, evidence-basis errors, and material coverage or scope losses. Counts concern distinct proposition/error/case groups; the ledger separately identifies affected runs. A shared error can affect both conditions. Convention deviations, defensible alternatives, and unresolved diagnoses remain separate. Every source entry, retained unit, relation, and outcome or mechanism claim enters the review, including claims on which all coders agree.

Agreement measures use the frozen correspondence between focal propositions. They report screening, exact-span matches, one-to-one semantic matches, and field-level unanimity. Split, combined, unmatched, and unresolved records remain visible in the coverage results. The common all-six subset permits comparison on the same propositions. The former scalar standing label and the new documentary/recognition/application profile do not receive a numerical crosswalk. A Boolean dispute flag also cannot represent the full scope of a challenge.

During execution, the author asked how human intercoder reliability would be assessed. A dated supplementary declaration added nominal Krippendorff alpha and pairwise agreement for the common categorical fields, before alignment or comparison of coded labels. These are supplementary descriptive measures, not prespecified acceptance thresholds. The analysis reports category distributions and undefined coefficients where all labels occupy a single category. Three clustered episodes do not support population reliability estimates, confidence intervals, or an AI-versus-human performance claim.
